Heritage walk in Patna: Pataliputra, gurdwaras and museums

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

A heritage walk in Patna follows ancient Pataliputra, capital of the Mauryas: the Kumhrar excavations with the remains of a pillared hall, Agam Kuan well, Takht Sri Harmandir Sahib (birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh), Golghar granary (1786), and the Bihar and Patna museums. Nalanda Mahavihara, a UNESCO site, is about 90 kilometres away.

We arrange heritage walks in Patna and trips to Nalanda and Rajgir on request for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, with an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi.

Why Patna matters for heritage

Patna is one of the longest continuously inhabited cities in the world. As Pataliputra it was the capital of Magadha under the Nandas, the Mauryas and later the Guptas, and the city that the Greek envoy Megasthenes described around 300 BCE, with timber walls and many gates along the Ganga. Much of that ancient city lies under the modern one, so archaeology here comes in windows: Kumhrar, Bulandi Bagh and other excavated spots.

The city is also a gateway. Nalanda, Rajgir, Vaishali and Bodh Gaya are within a few hours, and Patna's two major museums hold the best objects from all of them, including the Didarganj Yakshi. A school or college trip can begin in the museums and then go out to the sites. Our guide to heritage sites in Bihar maps the region.

Layers of history in Patna

Tradition credits Ajatashatru, king of Magadha in the 5th century BCE, with building a fort at the village of Pataligrama on the Ganga; his successor Udayin moved the capital here. Under Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka (4th to 3rd century BCE) Pataliputra became the political centre of an empire stretching from Afghanistan to the Deccan. The Mauryan empire and Ashoka and his edicts explainers tell that story.

The Guptas (4th to 6th century CE) also ruled from Pataliputra for a time, but by the time the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang visited in the 7th century much of it was in ruins. The city revived under Sher Shah Suri in the 1540s, who built a fort and the mosque that carries his name, and grew into a major Mughal trading city, Azimabad. Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, was born here in 1666.

From the 17th century European companies set up factories for saltpetre, cotton and opium; the Dutch and English buildings survive in parts of Gulzarbagh and the Collectorate. After 1912 Patna became the capital of the new province of Bihar and Orissa, and the British laid out a new administrative quarter in the west of the city.

Places a heritage walk in Patna covers

  1. Kumhrar Mauryan, about 4th to 3rd century BCE, with later layers

    Excavated remains of a pillared hall of Pataliputra, with a polished pillar on display.

  2. Agam Kuan Traditionally Mauryan

    Deep, brick-lined circular well linked in legend with Ashoka.

  3. Bulandi Bagh Mauryan

    Site where long stretches of the timber palisade of Pataliputra were found; little visible today but important to the story.

  4. Takht Sri Harmandir Sahib Gurdwara rebuilt in the 1950s on a 17th century site

    Birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh (1666), one of the five Takhts.

  5. Sher Shah Suri Masjid 1540s

    Mosque built under Sher Shah in Afghan style, in Patna City.

  6. Padri ki Haveli (St Mary's Church) 1772 rebuilding

    One of the oldest churches in Bihar, in Patna City.

  7. Gulzarbagh and the old opium factory 18th to 19th century

    Riverside buildings of the East India Company's opium trade, now a government press.

  8. Golghar 1786

    Beehive-shaped granary built after the famine of 1770, with stairs spiralling to the top.

  9. Patna Collectorate 18th century Dutch buildings onward

    Remains of Dutch trading buildings; part of a long heritage debate about redevelopment.

  10. Nalanda Mahavihara About 5th to 12th century CE

    UNESCO site with monasteries, temples and stupas; vehicle needed.

  11. Rajgir 6th century BCE onward

    Earlier Magadhan capital with cyclopean walls and Buddhist and Jain sites; vehicle needed.

  12. Vaishali 6th century BCE onward

    Ashokan lion pillar and stupa remains north of the Ganga; vehicle needed.

Walking routes in Patna

Pataliputra and the old city (vehicle between stops)

About 4 hours

Kumhrar → Agam Kuan → Bulandi Bagh → Takht Sri Harmandir Sahib → Sher Shah Suri Masjid → Padri ki Haveli (St Mary's Church)

The river and the Company city

About 2.5 hours

Gulzarbagh and the old opium factory → Patna Collectorate → Golghar

Nalanda and Rajgir (vehicle needed)

A full day

Nalanda Mahavihara → Rajgir

Museums in Patna

  • Bihar Museum. Modern museum opened in 2015 with galleries on early Bihar, the Mauryas, Buddhism and history, and the Didarganj Yakshi.
  • Patna Museum. Older museum (1917) in an Indo-Saracenic building with sculpture, coins, natural history and a relic casket from Vaishali.
  • Nalanda Archaeological Museum. ASI site museum at Nalanda with sculpture, seals and objects from the excavations.
  • Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Library. Major library of Arabic and Persian manuscripts and miniatures; check access for groups.

Best time for a walk

October to March. Summers are hot and the monsoon brings flooding along the Ganga; winter fog can delay travel in December and January.

What you see on a Patna heritage walk

At Kumhrar, excavations in 1912 to 1915 and 1951 to 1955 uncovered the remains of a large Mauryan pillared hall, with one polished sandstone pillar on display, and later Buddhist structures. It is the best place to explain how archaeologists find a city under a city. Agam Kuan, a deep brick-lined well traditionally linked with Ashoka, is nearby.

In the old city to the east (Patna City), the walk takes in Takht Sri Harmandir Sahib, one of the five Takhts of Sikhism, Sher Shah's mosque, and the riverfront. In the west, Golghar, a beehive-shaped granary built in 1786 after the famine of 1770, gives a view over the Ganga from its top. Our lecture Excavation headlines: evidence or exaggeration? is a good way to prepare students to think about what Kumhrar does and does not prove.

Day trips from Patna: Nalanda, Rajgir and Vaishali

Nalanda is about 90 kilometres south-east (2.5 to 3 hours by road). The excavated monasteries and temples of the Nalanda Mahavihara, active from about the 5th to 12th century CE, were inscribed by UNESCO in 2016. Our Nalanda: Monastic University Landscape programme takes groups through the site and its museum with an archaeologist. Rajgir, the older Magadhan capital with its cyclopean wall, is 15 kilometres beyond, and Vaishali, with an Ashokan lion pillar, is about 40 kilometres north across the Ganga.

These need a vehicle and usually a full day each. For a longer trip, Temples of eastern India and a study tour built for your group can combine Patna, Nalanda, Rajgir and Bodh Gaya.

Patna heritage walk for schools and groups

The city sites are spread out, so groups use a vehicle between Kumhrar, Patna City and Golghar and walk at each. Allow at least three hours at the Bihar Museum. Cover heads at the gurdwara, where volunteers welcome visitors. Talaash Heritage can begin the day with a short classroom session on the Mauryas and end it in the museum gallery.

Questions people ask

What are the main historical places in Patna?

Kumhrar (ancient Pataliputra), Agam Kuan, Takht Sri Harmandir Sahib, Sher Shah Suri Masjid, Padri ki Haveli, Golghar and the Patna and Bihar museums. Nalanda, Rajgir and Vaishali are day trips.

What can you see of ancient Pataliputra today?

Mainly the excavated site at Kumhrar, with the remains of a Mauryan pillared hall and one polished pillar, plus objects in the Bihar and Patna museums. Most of the ancient city lies under modern Patna.

How far is Nalanda from Patna?

About 90 kilometres, roughly 2.5 to 3 hours by road. Rajgir is a further 15 kilometres, so the two are usually visited together in a day.

Which museums in Patna are best for students?

The Bihar Museum for a clear story of the region from prehistory onwards, and the Patna Museum for its older collections. Allow half a day for the Bihar Museum alone.

Is Patna good for a school heritage trip?

Yes, especially combined with Nalanda and Rajgir. Students see the Mauryan capital, Sikh and Mughal heritage, and the colonial city in one day, and a great ancient monastic university the next.
